title: Texas' Top 50 BBQ joints from worst to best, according to ChatGPT
key_facts: Texas Monthly barbecue editor Daniel Vaughn criticised on social media an AI-made Top 50 Texas barbecue list that named closed places, wrong locations, an Arizona restaurant and places that do not exist.
MySA asked ChatGPT for its own Top 50, telling it not to copy Texas Monthly's 2025 list.
ChatGPT put CorkScrew BBQ in Spring, outside Houston, at No. 1 for "repeatability", and said it used data such as the 2026 Michelin Guide and regional criticism.
The list included Brotherton's Black Iron Barbecue, which closed on 30 Aug after almost a decade in Pflugerville.
ChatGPT claimed not to favour famous places, yet Leroy and Lewis, Burnt Bean, Goldee's, Truth and Tejas all landed in its top 10, as on Texas Monthly's list.
MySA concludes the chatbot visited no restaurant and spoke to no pitmaster, so its list is a guess based on other people's work.
quote_evidence: Brotherton's Black Iron Barbecue was included on the list despite closing on August 30.
The main thing to remember is ChatGPT did not do any of its own work.
If a real person had made this list, that would've been a fatal mistake.
why_it_matters_hint: A local test shows a chatbot ranking restaurants with out-of-date details.
event_date: Not stated (Vaughn's post described as recent); Brotherton's closed 30 Aug
notes: One prompt, one outlet; not a systematic study.
